slides.title: Historic Perspective: Symmetry Becomes A Design Rule
slides.notes: Open the lecture by treating the historical chapter as a compression of the whole course. The point is not to memorize names in sequence. The point is to see how symmetry, locality, spectra, graphs, and algorithms gradually turned into engineering constraints that can be checked in a model.

slides.title: Six Threads To Track
slides.notes: Use the route slide as a contract for attention. Each thread answers a different question: what transformations matter, which architecture inherited the idea, which expressivity test reveals a limit, which spectral tools explain filtering, which geometry processing ideas became neural layers, and which algorithmic invariants survive rollout.

slides.title: Symmetry History As A Model Contract
slides.notes: Frame the timeline as a change in vocabulary. Classical symmetry starts as visible regularity, becomes group action in mathematics, becomes conservation and gauge principle in physics, and then becomes a machine learning contract: an allowed transformation should either leave the output unchanged or move it predictably.

slides.title: Early Equivariance In Machine Learning
slides.notes: Emphasize the architectural lesson rather than the chronology alone. Single-layer invariance has sharp limitations, so useful models distribute the symmetry burden across local filters, hierarchy, pooling, and representation structure. CNNs are therefore not isolated inventions; they are one successful answer to the shift-symmetry problem.

slides.title: Graph Neural Networks Have Several Ancestors
slides.notes: This slide prevents a common false history in which GNNs appear suddenly in the late 2010s. The modern message-passing layer sits at the intersection of recursive neural networks, molecular graph models, random-walk embeddings, and probabilistic graphical model inference. Each ancestor contributes a different expectation about what an edge means.

slides.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman: Expressivity Becomes Inspectable
slides.notes: Slow down here because the WL example is the chapter's cleanest bridge from history to diagnostics. The two graphs are not isomorphic, yet 1-WL keeps producing the same color histogram. Message-passing GNNs with ordinary neighborhood aggregation inherit the same ceiling unless their inputs or update domain are strengthened.

slides.title: Harmonic Analysis Explains Filtering Beyond Grids
slides.notes: Connect the picture to the course's earlier grids, graphs, groups, and manifolds. Wavelets, scattering, and graph Fourier bases all ask how to decompose a signal into stable components. The historical importance is that convolutional success could be studied as filtering, not only as parameter fitting.

slides.title: Geometry Processing Supplies Intrinsic Operators
slides.notes: Treat meshes and point clouds as domains where coordinates are often nuisance data. Geometry processing contributed Laplacian spectra, geodesic patches, intrinsic descriptors, and local frames before these appeared as deep layers. The neural versions learn parts of the pipeline while still relying on the same intrinsic tests.

slides.title: Attention Recasts A Complete Graph As A Layer
slides.notes: Make the Transformer connection precise without overclaiming. A self-attention layer can be read as message passing on a complete graph whose edge weights are inferred from features. That does not make every Transformer a geometric model automatically, but it explains why graph language and attention language keep meeting.

slides.title: Algorithmic Reasoning Uses Invariants Over Time
slides.notes: Shift from spatial geometry to computational geometry of information flow. In an algorithm, edges may describe data dependencies rather than similarity or proximity. The invariant is temporal: after each step, a predicate about partial progress should remain true, and a learned processor must preserve that predicate outside the training sizes.

slides.title: A Historical Blueprint For New Architectures
slides.notes: Use this synthesis slide to turn history into a design checklist. A new architecture should declare its domain, allowed transformations, local operator, aggregation rule, readout, and failure probe. The historical references matter because they show where each checklist item came from and what can go wrong when it is missing.

slides.title: Takeaway: Geometry Is The Audit Trail
slides.notes: Close by returning to the notebook's lab habit. Break a symmetry assumption, perturb a graph, rotate coordinates, change a frame, or scale the input size, then inspect the residual. The chapter's historical perspective is ultimately practical: geometric language turns architectural claims into tests a learner can run.
